thread:
Nora (product): quick design/ops question — we keep getting support tickets where customers say they clicked 'Rollback' but can't find who triggered it in the timeline. can we agree a pattern: show initiator, op-id, and keyboard focus chain for the rollback flow? figma: https://figma.redwood/rollback-audit-v1
Ethan (design): good call. my design goal: make the actor and op-id discoverable without crowding the row. proposal: small condensed 'meta' line under the version row: 'rolled back by Maya • op-6642' that expands on hover.
Riley (frontend): implementation notes: expand-on-hover is fine for mouse, but we need keyboard-friendly affordance. plan: an inline disclosure button (aria-expanded) that toggles the meta row. default collapsed for density. also add a tiny copy-to-clipboard for op-id.
Sam (eng-runtime): backend can provide actor, op-id, timestamp, and team id. we'll include a linkable operation URL. caution: op-ids can be long; truncate visually but keep full text in sr-only and clipboard action.
Jas (a11y): accessibility constraints: the disclosure must be reachable by keyboard and announce expanded state with aria-live polite. When a rollback happens live, the new row must not steal focus unless user invoked it. For explicit user actions (they clicked rollback) the confirmation overlay should move focus to the new operation status and create an accessible live region summarizing who started it. sample SR text: 'Rollback to v2.9 initiated by Alex at 14:12 UTC. operation id op-6642.'
Nora (product): UX question: should the meta line show on all rollback rows or only when hovered/focused? I worry about visual clutter when there are many rows.
Ethan (design): default collapsed, but for any row with a recent change (within 24h) auto-expand. visual style: micro-muted text and subtle chevron. add hover target to reveal full label. keep contrast high.
Riley (frontend): for small screens collapse meta into a single kebab menu entry 'Details' that opens a stacked panel. keyboard: arrow keys should navigate rows; when a row is 'selected' show meta details in a side rail to avoid reflow.
Sam (eng-runtime): support wants op-id in the toast too: when rollback starts show 'Rollback started — op-6642 · View operation' with a shallow link. can emit a short-lived event that AuditBot can pick up.
AuditBot: Operation op-6642 started by maya@redwood (team core-platform) · ETA ~95s · link: https://ops.redwood/ops/op-6642
Jas (a11y): SR testing notes: live announcements must be precise but not noisy. For automatic auto-expand rows only use polite announcements: 'v2.9 rolled back by Maya' and provide a visible 'Details' button for users to request full op-id. For user-initiated flows use assertive: 'Rollback started by you — op-6642'.
Nora (product): copy micro-decisions to confirm: 1) show actor + op-id in meta row (collapsed by default) 2) auto-expand recent change rows (<24h) 3) copy-to-clipboard for op-id + toast 4) side-rail details on small screens 5) SR: polite for automatic updates, assertive for user-initiated. thumbs?
Ethan (design): :+1: on all 5
Riley (frontend): :+1: will prototype disclosure + clipboard button, side-rail on mobile
Sam (eng-runtime): :+1: will add op-url to operation payload and emit AuditBot event
Jas (a11y): :+1: will author SR copy and test with screen readers
Nora (product): action items: Ethan update figma + collapsed meta spec; Riley prototype keyboard + clipboard + side-rail; Sam include op-url & short op-id format; Jas produce SR text bundle. I'll collate into the rollback UX brief. Thanks team!
